findings.title: A policy waiver of a rule that a two-rule scan also enforces now throws, for any target
findings.after:
for rule in rules_for_scan(id)
        rule == canonical && continue
        e = first(Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy"), 1)
        isempty(e) || throw(Ledger.LedgerError("$rule on $(e[1]["target"]) is a policy waiver of a rule $id enforces but does not own ..."))
findings.why_it_matters: A consumer ledger entry that base accepted now breaks the build. Take `id = "RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING", scope = "policy", target = "docs/src/api/Foo.md"`. Base let it through CFG.EXEMPTIONS and SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE ignored it, because its target is not `*`. At head it throws LedgerError. apply_ledger runs outside run_scan's try and the scan is hard tier, so makedocs' `scan_docs(cfg; hard_only = true)` crashes and CFG.EXEMPTIONS FAILs. The same happens for RULE.CIT.DOI (hard DOI_CROSSCHECK) and RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE. RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING is also the canonical rule of SCAN.HTML_DOCSTRING_ONCE, HTML_PUBLIC_HOME and HTML_BASE_LEAK. RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE's check includes `panel`. So these three rules can no longer be declared as policy deviations at all. The remedy the message names, `scope = "scan"`, waives the canonical rule too, which is the over-wide result the change says it ends. policy/00-index.md says 'a rule a package deviates from is a ledger entry'; that now fails for three rules.
findings.description: The defect was that a target-`*` waiver of the second rule disabled the whole scan. The fix is wider than that. It refuses every live policy entry on the second rule, whatever its target or match, and it refuses before any hit is seen. The docstring, the RULES.toml comments and the test were rewritten in the same window to call the refusal the contract. At base the over-wide disable was recorded as a known limit, and entries on specific targets never reached the scan.
findings.evidence: Scan.jl head: `e = first(Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy"), 1)` (no target filter). run_scan: `catch err; err isa Ledger.LedgerError && rethrow()` wraps only `f(cfg, files)`; `kept, exempted, disabled = apply_ledger(...)` sits outside the try. catalog/scans.toml: SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE `tier = "hard"`, SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK `tier = "hard"`; SCAN.HTML_DOCSTRING_ONCE/PUBLIC_HOME/BASE_LEAK `rule = "RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING"`. RULES.toml: RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE `check = ["scan:SCAN.DEAD_REF", "panel"]`. Running unreachable_waiver_scans over the register gives RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING => [SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE], RULE.CIT.DOI => [SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK], RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE => [SCAN.DEAD_REF]. docs/src/guide/ledger.md: an `[exemption.match]` table 'refines a `scan`, `lint`, `policy` or `harness` entry'.

findings.title: FROZEN_MIDROUND gains an exception whose stated condition the verb never checks
findings.before: statement = "An instrument is never changed mid-round; a change is its own commit and release; a deferral is written in the round's deferred.md and carried into the work queue at close."
findings.after: statement = "... ; a round whose own frozen scripts cannot run has the differing copies replaced by gbg round scripts --reason, recorded in ROUND.toml."  /  "One relaxation is recorded rather than hidden: a round whose own frozen Workflow scripts cannot run — its verifiers unparseable, so it could never verify — has the differing copies replaced"  /  "This verb is the one exception, and it is narrow."
findings.why_it_matters: The fleet rulebook, rendered into every consumer's CLAUDE.md, now allows mid-round script replacement when 'its verifiers [are] unparseable'. The code does not test that condition. `gbg round scripts <round> --reason "<any 24 characters>"` replaces every script that differs from the running copy, including the instrument's own lens (lanes.js, panel.js, audit.js, hunt.js). In the dev checkout the running copy is the working tree. So a check-docs round of the tool, opened at a tag, can take a lens edited on master after preflight through this verb. CLAUDE.md forbids exactly that: 'a change to a scan, a script ... never folded into a round it scores'. The record (from/to shas, after_pass) makes the change visible, but the rule's text says it is limited to unrunnable verifiers, and it is not.
findings.description: The base verb existed and re-copied every script unconditionally, which contradicted a policy that allowed no exception. Head narrows the verb by requiring a reason and replacing only scripts that differ. But it settles the contradiction by rewriting the rule to admit a relaxation, and the text describes that relaxation more narrowly than the code implements it. A related detail: the refresh_scripts docstring says `Preflight.copy_scripts` 'runs at preflight, and otherwise only here'. At head the verb calls install_script, and copy_scripts's only caller is Preflight.jl:969.
findings.evidence:
Rounds.jl head: `for (name, src) in Preflight.script_sources(String(rec["instrument"]))
 dst = joinpath(wdir, name); new = Preflight.render_script(src)
 old = isfile(dst) ? sha(read(dst)) : "absent"
 old == sha(new) && continue ... Preflight.install_script(src, dst)`. The only gate: `length(strip(reason)) >= 24`. Preflight.script_sources: `out = [(f, joinpath(src, f)) for f in readdir(src) if endswith(f, ".js")]` — the instrument's own scripts first. `rg copy_scripts src` -> only `src/CLI/Preflight.jl:969: scripts = copy_scripts(cfg, instrument, round)`.

findings.title: round.schema tightened in place, and a tool-written record it refuses is reported as exit 2
findings.after: "required": ["at", "head", "reason", "after_pass", "scripts"]  /  "pattern": "^([0-9a-f]{64}|)$"  /  # a record the schema refuses (one an earlier tool wrote, or a hand edit) is "cannot evaluate" for every round verb — exit 2 ... err isa ErrorException || rethrow(); throw(RoundError(err.msg))
findings.why_it_matters: `gbg round scripts` has shipped since v1.0.0-rc.9 (6bf4571) and wrote `{at, head}` entries. Any ROUND.toml holding such an entry, open or closed, now fails validation. RoundFiles.rounds marks it `:invalid`, gate_problems sets `fatal`, and Pkg.test()'s gate and every makedocs gate exit 2. `close` and `abandon` on that round exit 2 too, and ROUND.toml is 'never edited by hand', so no verb can clear it. schema_version stays 1 even though 'Every artefact carries schema_version (= the tool's MAJOR)'. Separately, `config_sha = ""` is now schema-valid for every round, not only for the Step-0 import that needed it.
findings.description: Adding required fields makes records written by rc.9 to rc.11 invalid. The new catch in `load` explicitly routes 'one an earlier tool wrote' to exit 2 without a backtrace. The same diff argues the opposite for configs: 'A config this tool has just written failing to validate is a defect of the tool, not of the consumer, so it must reach the crash path'. The catch also turns every ErrorException from read_round into a consumer-side 'cannot evaluate'. Whether any live record carries an old-shape entry could not be checked, because round files are out of this lane's reach.
findings.evidence: RoundFiles.read_round: `isempty(errs) || error("$(p) is invalid:\n  " * join(errs, "\n  "))`. RoundFiles.rounds: `catch err; (nothing, :invalid)`. Gate.gate_problems: `if r.state in (:nomarker, :invalid) ... fatal = true`. `git tag --contains 6bf4571` -> v1.0.0-rc.9, rc.10, rc.11. Config.jl head docstring for ConfigWrittenError: 'a defect of the tool, not of the consumer, so it must reach the crash path — exit 3 with its backtrace'.

findings.title: latex_source_globs flipped from replacing the default surfaces to adding to them
findings.before:
"the AUTHORED SOURCE a hat whose needs include `source` is sent to, repo-relative — the consumer's globs when it set any, the four default surfaces otherwise."
        a["source_globs"] = isempty(globs) ? ["src", "ext", "docs/src", "docs"] : globs
findings.after:
"the four default surfaces (src, ext, docs/src, docs) followed by every glob the consumer names — added to them, never in place of them."
source_globs(cfg::AbstractDict) =
    unique!(vcat(SOURCE_SURFACES, String.(get(cfg["instruments"]["check-consistency"], "latex_source_globs", String[]))))
findings.why_it_matters: The migration design gives CP `latex_source_globs = ["src/*.jl"]` (ARCHITECTURE:1359). At base its `needs: source` hats read only `src/*.jl`. At head they read src, ext, docs/src, docs and src/*.jl, and CP's pass verifier's source_scope changes the same way (base: the four literals). A consumer can no longer narrow the source a hat reads. The key's only documented meaning, the instrument schema description, was rewritten to the opposite semantics, and config.schema.json still gives the key no description.
findings.description: The replacement semantics were the documented contract at base, where the reader was introduced. Head reverses them to a union and rewrites the description and the test to match. It cites an audit that saw the replacement as a cut. That may be the right design. Still, it is a change to what a configured value does, made silently in both directions within two windows, and there is no longer any form of the key that narrows.
findings.evidence: git show 3e30907:src/CLI/Preflight.jl render_args: `globs = String.(get(cfg["instruments"]["check-consistency"], "latex_source_globs", String[]))\n a["source_globs"] = isempty(globs) ? ["src", "ext", "docs/src", "docs"] : globs`. schema/config.schema.json:441 `"latex_source_globs": {"$ref": "#/$defs/strlist", "default": []}` (no description). test/coverage.jl head: `@test G.Preflight.source_globs(cfg) == ["src", "ext", "docs/src", "docs", "src/*.jl", "examples/*.jl"]`.

findings.title: Claim checklist's quantifier class cut by half; guide exit-contract line dropped
findings.before:
Narrowed to a quantifier in a line that also names a tool identifier — where a universal is a claim ABOUT this tool
const CLAIM_QUANTIFIER = r"\b(?:every|never|always|all|none|any|only)\b"i
const CLAIM_TOOL_ID = r"...|\bgbg\s+[a-z]+\b"
findings.after:
Narrowed to a strong universal (`every`, `never`, `always`, `none` — not `all`, `any` or `only` ...) in the same CLAUSE as a register id or a backticked `gbg` verb ... The per-lane counts before and after that narrowing are in the commit that made it (2026-09-15).
const CLAIM_TOOL_ID = r"...|`gbg\s+[a-z]+"
findings.why_it_matters: I ran both versions over src, ext, docs/src, policy, instruments, catalog, templates and ARCHITECTURE.md. Quantifier items fell from 481 to 228, and 114 of the dropped lines still carry every/never/always/none. They fall out because the gbg verb is not backticked or a ' — ' splits the clause. One example is Passes.jl:479 'gbg round close $round carries every id still open into the next $inst round', a universal about the tool in a single clause. The exit class also loses docs/src/guide/verbs.md:7 'The exit contract is one for all: `0`', the guide's own statement of the exit contract, because a code in a code span no longer satisfies `[0-3]\s+[a-z]`. The fix for a version-string false positive only needed the `(?<![\w.])` lookbehind. The lanes owe a verdict only on listed items, so this checklist narrowing reduces what an audit is obliged to check.
findings.description: The comment keeps the promise that the class targets claims about the tool, but the new tool-id test and clause split exclude such claims written in plain text. The evidence for the cut is sent to a commit message rather than kept with the code.
findings.evidence: Base-vs-head regex run: `exit old=213 new=212 ; quantifier old=481 new=228 ; lost lines carrying a strong universal: 114`; exit lost: `docs/src/guide/verbs.md:7`; quantifier lost includes `src/CLI/Passes.jl:479: println(io, "pass open: refused — the pass budget is spent ($used of $cap). gbg round close $round carries every id still open into the next $inst round.")`.

findings.title: A count base deliberately kept out of ARCHITECTURE is back, justified by a false 'every count'
findings.before: `SCAN.SIGNATURE_TYPED` re-measures it on every run, so no count is carried here to go stale
findings.after: measured on 2026-09-12, 247 of 251, the other four corrected when the rule was narrowed; ... Those figures are that day's snapshot, as every count in this document is dated
findings.why_it_matters: At base the text said no count would be carried, so that none could go stale. Head adds a figure that nothing in the tree can re-derive; the scan measures today's tree, not 2026-09-12's. It supports the figure with a universal claim that is false: ARCHITECTURE has undated counts, for example 'Twenty-two schemas' (§D11, line 645) and 'PF 6 surfaces, IT 4, SS 4' (§5 table).
findings.description: The row was rewritten to put back a measurement the base design had removed on purpose. The universal claim added to excuse it does not hold for the document it describes.
findings.evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:645 `**Choice.** Twenty-two schemas: ...` (undated); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:100 `PF 6 surfaces, IT 4, SS 4 (survey-checkdocs.md:51)` (undated).
